name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Yadadri
description:
The Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple at Yadadri (historically known as Yadagirigutta) is celebrated as a major spiritual center of Sanatana Dharma. Located in the Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana, this ancient hill shrine is designated as a Pancha Narasimha Kshetram—a sacred site where Lord Vishnu manifested in five distinct self-manifested (Swayambhu) forms.

The Five Manifestations (Swayambhu Cave Deities)
Unlike temples with sculpted idols, the sanctum sanctorum of Yadadri is a natural cavern housing five forms of the deity:
Jwala Narasimha: Represented as a column of divine fire. According to legend, when the heat of this manifestation became too intense, Lord Vishnu softened His form.
Yogananda Narasimha: Seated in a peaceful, meditative yogic posture, representing the Lord teaching the spiritual path to His devotees.
Gandabherunda Narasimha: Naturally engraved on the rocky cave wall, representing the two-headed bird avatar.
Ugra Narasimha: The fierce, protective aspect of the Lord, emerging to destroy evil.
Lakshmi Narasimha: A benign, peaceful form with Goddess Lakshmi seated on His lap, blessing devotees with prosperity.

The Architectural Marvel (YTDA Krishna Shila Reconstruction)
The reconstruction of the Yadadri temple is one of the largest stone temple renovation projects in modern history. Executed by the Yadadri Temple Development Authority (YTDA) and designed by chief architect Anand Sai and traditional sthapatis, the temple has been expanded from a 2-acre hill shrine to a sprawling 17-acre stone complex.
Key Architectural Highlights
Krishna Shila (Black Granite): Built entirely out of black granite stone sourced from Guntur and Prakasam districts (Andhra Pradesh). Over 2.5 lakh tonnes of stone were hand-carved by 2,500 sculptors. Black granite was chosen because it absorbs liquids like milk, curd, and oil, becoming harder and stronger over centuries.
Traditional Lime Mortar: No cement, concrete, or bricks were used in the main temple structure. Instead, a traditional mix of lime, jaggery, inknut (karakkaya), aloe vera, and coconut jute mortar was used, which grows stronger over centuries.
Seven Gopurams: The complex is crowned with seven majestic gopurams, including the gold-plated Vimana Gopuram above the sanctum sanctorum, built entirely of stone from base to top.
Alvar pillars: The outer walkways (Maha Mandapam) feature carved pillars depicting the 12 Alvar saints of the Vaishnavite tradition.

mythology: As recorded in the Skanda Purana, during the Treta Yuga, the son of Sage Rishyasringa, named Yada Rishi, came to this hill to perform intense penance. Pleased with his devotion and guided by the blessings of Lord Anjaneya (Hanuman), Lord Vishnu appeared before him. The Lord manifested in these five forms. At the sage's request, the Lord permanently resided on the hill inside the cavern to bless humanity.

sub_temples.name: Sri Ramalingeshwara Swamy Temple
sub_temples.description: Located on the same hillock, representing the harmonious coexistence of Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions.

sub_temples.name: Patha Gutta Temple (Old Temple)
sub_temples.description: Located 2 km from the main hill, this is the original site of worship before the main temple's modern reconstruction.
